newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end higher, boosted by drugs.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end higher, boosted by drugs.

text.p: Swedish share prices ended slightly higher on Monday after a trendless day, bolstered by a rise in the drugs sector.
The Stockholm Stock Exchange general index ended 0.1 percent higher at 2,756.61 in turnover of 4.5 billion crowns.
Drug company Astra rose 4.5 crowns to 315.5 on persistent rumours that a foreign drug company was interested in taking it over.
Pharmacia & Upjohn shares closed up 15.5 crowns to 259 after a conference call with the company's new chief executive officer, Fred Hassan.
Hassan said he expected 1998 to be a better year than 1997.

"Naturally this is good news and many investors have returned to the share...It's U.S. investors who above all are pushing the share. They have traded more shares in one hour in New York than what we have done all day," a broker said.
Car safety equipment maker Autoliv jumped eleven crowns to 290 on interest from U.S. investors, brokers said.
Pricer, which makes data systems for reading bar codes, rose 17 crowns to 276.
